title: Global 10M QPS Real-Time Bidding Ad Auction with 10ms Hard Deadline
subtitle: Tail Latency Amplification Mitigation, Request Hedging and Budget Pacing
problem_statement: An ad-tech exchange executes 10 million real-time bidding auctions per second. For each impression, the exchange fans out bid requests to 50 downstream Demand-Side Platforms (DSPs). Downstream DSPs have variable tail latencies, causing 35% of auctions to miss the strict 10-millisecond hard deadline, resulting in zero revenue.

faded_bug.description: Waiting for slow DSPs synchronously without dynamic outlier shedding drops entire auction revenue.

studio_1_runtime.correct_fix_diff:
+ // Implement dynamic circuit breaking: skip DSPs whose rolling P99 exceeds 8ms
+ if dspHealth.IsDegraded(dsp) { continue }

invariants.description: Auction must execute and return winning bid in <= 10.0ms at P99.99.

probing_ladder.stage_1_validation: Explain the Tail Latency Amplification formula: $P(\text{system delayed}) = 1 - (1 - p)^N$. Why does fanning out to 50 DSPs with $p=99\%$ yield a $40\%$ system-wide delay probability?
probing_ladder.stage_2_tightening: How do you implement Request Hedging or tied-requests with cancellation without doubling traffic on downstream bidders?
probing_ladder.stage_3_adversarial: A bidder has an algorithmic bug and always returns bids at 10.01ms. How does your adaptive score ranker evict slow DSPs to protect auction yield?
probing_ladder.stage_4_squeeze: How do you maintain real-time advertiser budget pacing (spending $100,000 evenly across 24 hours) across 10M QPS without lock contention?

counter_probes.counter_question: If you wait for all 50 DSPs, your latency is dictated by the single slowest server in the entire internet ecosystem. What happens to your 10ms publisher SLA?
counter_probes.expected_staff_answer: The SLA will be breached in 40%+ of cases. An RTB exchange must enforce a hard cut-off timer at 9ms, auctioning among whoever replied in time and pruning chronic stragglers.
